evals.name: set-up-statusline-for-new-project
evals.prompt: I just started a new Node.js project. Help me set up a Claude Code statusline that shows the current model, working directory, git branch (with dirty marker), and an npm-script-runner health dot. The script should live at scripts/statusline/statusline.sh and .claude/settings.json should reference it via ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}.
evals.expected_output: A complete statusline script with: (1) the .claude/settings.json statusLine entry using ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}, (2) the statusline.sh script in scripts/statusline/ with at least model + cwd + git segments, (3) graceful degradation when jq/npm are missing, (4) NO_COLOR handling, (5) no [ ! -t 1 ] TTY check (that would strip colors when Claude Code pipes the output).

evals.name: add-docker-segment
evals.prompt: My statusline shows model, cwd, git, and pm2 services. Add a new segment that shows whether the Docker daemon is up (a green dot if `docker info` succeeds, red if it doesn't). Make it fault-tolerant — if docker is not installed, just hide the segment.
evals.expected_output: A new SEG_DOCKER block following the existing pattern in the statusline script: guard on `command -v docker`, then `docker info >/dev/null 2>&1` to test, set the segment with green/red dots using the existing C_GREEN/C_RED constants, append to the final LINE composition. No restructuring of the rest of the script.

evals.name: fix-missing-colors
evals.prompt: My statusline shows up in the Claude Code terminal but has no colors. The script is at scripts/statusline/statusline.sh. I checked with cat -v and the script DOES emit \033[38;5;39m sequences in the file, but the rendered terminal output is plain text. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Diagnose: the script likely has a TTY-stripping guard like `if [ ! -t 1 ]` that disables colors when stdout is not a TTY. Claude Code invokes the statusline via pipe, so stdout is not a TTY. Fix: remove the `[ ! -t 1 ]` check, gate colors only on NO_COLOR per the no-color.org spec. Verify with `cat -v` on piped output to confirm SGR sequences are still present.

evals.name: pm2-env-leak
evals.prompt: I added a statusline that shows PM2 service status. A teammate ran `pm2 jlist > /tmp/jlist.json` and noticed the file contains DB_PASSWORD, JWT_SECRET, and NACOS_PASSWORD in `.pm2_env.env`. The statusline reads the same data on every tick. Audit the statusline script and tell me what to fix.
evals.expected_output: Identify the leak: the jq query that selects PM2 status probably projects more than `.name` and `.pm2_env.status`. The `.pm2_env.env` field is a string→string map of all process env vars. Fix: narrow the jq projection to ONLY the fields the statusline needs (`.name`, `.pm2_env.status`). Add a SECURITY comment in the script explaining why the projection must stay narrow. Verify by running the script and checking that no env-var values appear in the output.
